post.headline: Edo: 6 Months No Quit Notice If You Pay In Advance
lines: Ngozi, if you just paid your rent in Edo State, know your right.
The law says your landlord cannot issue a notice to quit for the first six months of your tenancy,
This gives you statutory breathing space, except by tribunal order or your consent.
Don't let anyone push you out before time.

threads.text: In Edo State, if you pay rent in advance for a monthly or quarterly tenancy, your landlord cannot give you a notice to quit for the first six months (s.18). This is your statutory breathing space. No landlord should force you out before then. Which state protects tenants best?
threads.evening: Edo tenants who pay rent upfront get a 6-month shield against quit notices. Know the law, protect your stay.

short.title: Paid a caution fee? Take photos on day one.
short.hook_say: Before you move into that new apartment, especially if you paid a caution fee, there's one critical thing to do. Many tenants forget this, and it costs them dearly later. Avoid paying for damages you didn't cause.

tips.say: Take clear photos or a video of every single crack, stain, or scratch in the apartment. Document the kitchen, bathroom, walls, and floors thoroughly. This is your evidence.
Ensure your photos and videos are dated, either by your phone's timestamp or a physical newspaper in the shot. This proves the condition of the property on your move-in day.

Send these dated photos or videos to your landlord or agent via WhatsApp or email. This creates a record that they received and acknowledged the initial state of the property. Keep your own copy safe.
